uncited: This family converts 2D rasterized surface data into 3D voxel grids by transferring world-space positions from a 2D texture (the "position map") into a 3D volume texture.
It solves the problem of efficiently populating a 3D grid from 2D rasterization outputs, avoiding the computational cost of geometric intersection tests in 3D space.
It differs from sibling methods by decoupling the rasterization of geometry (or instances) from the voxelization of the resulting surface points, using image-space coordinates as the bridge.
**Position Map Generation:** Rasterize geometry (triangles or billboards) into a 2D texture (`positionMap`) where each texel stores the world-space position of the nearest surface fragment.
**Volume Population:** Read the `positionMap` and map the stored world-space positions to 3D voxel indices.
This is done by rendering a full-screen quad and, for each fragment, converting the sampled world position $(pos.x, pos.y, pos.z)$ to voxel indices $(x, y, z)$ using the volume bounds and resolution.
*   **Boundary Conditions:** Positions outside the volume bounds result in negative or out-of-bounds indices.
The core concept of using position maps for voxelization is widely used in real-time graphics for collision detection and volumetric rendering.
